hypothesis: On a 4-state Markov world with V={0,1,2}, unviable={3}, uniform random policy over actions {stay, move}, and per-step leakage rate beta=0.05 by construction, Theorem AG-1 predicts survival probability Pr[q(X_t) in V for all t <= T] >= (1-beta)^T at every T; on this world the bound is tight at every T. Theorem AG-2 predicts survival is trivially 1.0 when V is enlarged to Z (everything viable).

controls.description: Every row of the induced 4x4 policy-averaged transition matrix sums to 1.0 (probability normalisation); checked in tests.
The (3, 3) entry of the kernel equals 1.0 and all other entries in row 3 equal 0.0; the unviable state is absorbing so 'stays in V for all t' equals 'never visits 3'.
Matrix powers are computed by repeated multiplication in pure Python; no randomness; identical output on every run.
Every row of the sub-matrix P_V on V sums to 1-beta=0.95 exactly (LEAK holds with equality uniformly), so the AG-1 bound is tight by construction on this world.

gates.criterion: For every T in {1, 3, 5, 10, 20}, exact survival probability under the coarse Markov kernel restricted to V is >= (1 - beta)^T.
At T=1, exact survival probability equals (1 - beta) = 0.95 exactly (within 1e-12).
When V is extended to V'=Z={0,1,2,3} (everything viable), the exact survival probability is 1.0 at every T (within 1e-12).
Exact survival probability on V is weakly monotone non-increasing across the horizon sweep {1, 3, 5, 10, 20}.
